title: Offline egress emulation and upgrade gates for VPC/private deployments
creator: Evan Brooks
description:
Problem: Customers running Redwood Private in isolated VPCs and air-gapped environments frequently cannot perform live upgrades or validate egress rules against production endpoints. This causes upgrade failures, long maintenance windows, and manual runbooks.

Goal: Define requirements and acceptance criteria for an "egress emulation" test harness and deterministic upgrade gating mechanism that operators can run inside customer networks prior to an upgrade. The feature should catch common networking/egress failure modes, validate proxy/whitelist rules, and produce a machine-readable verification artifact (upgrade checkpoint) that the Redwood control plane or on-prem orchestration tool can consume to allow/deny upgrades.

Scope: This ticket focuses on product requirements and acceptance criteria. Implementation will coordinate with ENG for an agent-side test harness, and with Console for UX to surface gating results and suggested remediation steps. Excluded: telemetry export from customer network to Redwood hosted analytics (must remain optional and documented separately).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Egress Emulation Harness: provide a portable test harness (containerized) that runs a standard suite of network checks inside a private deployment. Checks include DNS resolution for critical hostnames, TLS handshake validation against Redwood artifact mirrors, HTTP(S) connectivity to repo mirrors, outbound proxy authentication flow, and simulated artifact download (large binary stream) to verify throughput and timeout behavior.

2) Deterministic Checkpoint Artifact: the harness must produce a signed JSON checkpoint file containing test results, timestamps, deterministic hashes of artifacts fetched, and a concise pass/fail status for each sub-check. The file format must be documented and stable across minor releases.

3) Upgrade Gate Integration: the orchestrator must accept the checkpoint artifact and block an upgrade if any critical check failed. There must be at least two gate modes: strict (block on any critical failure) and advisory (warn and continue). Gate mode must be configurable per-deployment.

4) Clear Remediation Guidance: for each failed check, the harness must include actionable remediation text and links to runbook docs. Console must display failures with suggested fixes and a one-click re-run action (in environments where the agent can reach Redwood control plane).

5) Air-gapped Mode: the harness must support an offline-only mode where all tests use local mirrors and pre-seeded manifests. In offline mode, the checkpoint must still be verifiable by the orchestrator without outbound egress.

6) Security and Signing: checkpoint artifacts must be signed using customer-provided keys or a Redwood-specified container keypair; signature verification must be part of the upgrade gate. All network test tooling must avoid leaking customer secrets and must run at non-privileged user levels where possible.

7) Test Coverage and CI: ENG must provide unit and integration tests covering failure modes (DNS blocked, proxy auth failures, slow download) with >=90% deterministic test reliability.

8) Documentation and Runbooks: publish a runbook including expected failure fingerprints, remediation steps, and example checkpoint artifacts. Docs must include an offline-playbook for air-gapped customers.

9) Backwards Compatibility: older agents (within one major release) should still run the harness but must surface a compatibility-warning in the checkpoint.

10) Observability: harness run must emit an audit entry in local logs with run metadata; if external telemetry is enabled, an anonymized summary may be uploaded (opt-in).
notes_and_discussion: 2026-02-26: Kickoff with ENG networking and security — agreed to prototype a containerized harness (ENG-8124).
2026-03-02: PM-led scoping meeting — narrowed checks to DNS/TLS/HTTP proxy/auth/download/timeouts for MVP.
2026-03-05: Security flagged signing requirement; options: customer key upload or PKI via airgapped signing token. Follow-up with Security team scheduled.
2026-03-08: Design asked for UX wireframe for gate modes and re-run flow; Console PO assigned for collaboration.
2026-03-10: Added air-gapped mode acceptance criteria after a customer interview with a regulated healthcare provider requesting offline-only verification.

Open question: If the harness discovers intermittent failures (flaky DNS), should the checkpoint include historical samples or require X consecutive runs to pass? Proposal: require 3 runs by default for advisory mode; configurable by operator.
customer_examples: Customer A: large financials tenant had a failed upgrade due to a corporate proxy returning 407 for artifact downloads; harness should detect proxy auth flows and certificate re-signing needs.

Customer B: regional government cluster with split-horizon DNS that resolved internal repo hostnames incorrectly leading to checksum mismatches during image pull. Harness should flag DNS mismatches and include resolved IPs in checkpoint.
